review_mode: Read-only source review; only this report is written in the repository.
verdict: Two actionable findings: one structural coupling issue and one low-severity domain error-atomicity defect. No demonstrated authentication or tenant-isolation bypass in assigned files. Baseline system gates belong to the separate verification owner.

findings.title: Project use cases require the entire membership and organization mutation surface

evidence.detail: TenantTransaction inherits OrganizationRepository, ProjectRepository and MembershipRepository; every UnitOfWork returns this all-capabilities object.
The project-only fake must implement unrelated organization and membership capabilities with unimplemented! panics. The comments explicitly say those capabilities are unsupported.
Membership service imports the project module UoW despite not using project persistence.

authority: docs/spec/41105668422d81c183c3f9c30cc2ffd6.md:13-23 calls for narrow ports and transaction-scoped repositories, with signatures justified by ergonomics.
docs/adr-001.md:7 describes purpose-specific ports sharing a transaction; a single concrete SQL transaction is justified, but universal consumer capabilities are not required for atomicity.
findings.consequence: Any new membership capability forces project-only adapters and tests to change; unsupported operations compile and panic instead of being absent from the consumer contract. The nominally separate repository traits do not isolate consumers because the UoW immediately combines them. This is concrete cross-feature coupling, not a complaint about directory names or sharing one transaction.
findings.proposed_remedy: Keep the same concrete SQLx TenantWork and atomic commit owner. Narrow the transaction capability returned to each workflow (project, membership, organization/discovery), using small consumer-specific factory/transaction interfaces or an equivalently simple associated-type bound. Share only genuinely common authority/audit/commit capabilities. Delete the project fake membership and unused organization stubs. Do not introduce independent commits, generic repository frameworks, service locators or a layer per entity; accept the restructuring only if it removes unsupported surface and net test machinery.

findings.title: An exhausted project version returns Conflict after changing the name

evidence.detail: rename assigns self.name on line 61 before checked_add can return Conflict on line 62.
Tests cover stale version and successful rename, but never version exhaustion or the full unchanged object after a rejected command.
Current application caller propagates the error and drops the local object before save; there is no demonstrated persisted HTTP mutation from this defect.

findings.consequence: The public domain operation reports failure while retaining part of the rejected mutation. A caller retaining/retrying the aggregate observes a name change at the old version. Practical reach is limited to an exhausted i64 version or constructed/restored state, so this is not a production data-corruption claim.
findings.proposed_remedy: Compute the checked next version into a local before mutating either field, then assign name and version together. Add a rejection-atomicity test for stale version, invalid name and exhausted version that checks name, version and identity remain unchanged.

executable_verification.regression: Construct Project with name Before and version i64::MAX; call rename(i64::MAX, After); assert Err(Error::Conflict), name Before and version i64::MAX. This desired-behavior regression must fail before the fix and pass after it.
executable_verification.observed_probe: Compiled a standalone stdin Rust probe against the actual domain rlib with rustc +1.99.1. It asserted the defect (Err(Conflict) and name After), and exited 0. Output: result=Err(Conflict) name=After version=9223372036854775807
executable_verification.probe_kind: Defect-observing probe, not a desired-behavior GREEN test.
executable_verification.probe_source: extern crate domain; use domain::{Project,Error}; fn main(){let mut p=Project{id: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001".parse::<uuid::Uuid>().unwrap().into(),organization_id: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002".parse::<uuid::Uuid>().unwrap().into(),name:String::from("Before"),version:i64::MAX,archived:false}; let result=p.rename(i64::MAX,String::from("After")); println!("result={:?} name={} version={}",result,p.name,p.version); assert_eq!(result,Err(Error::Conflict)); assert_eq!(p.name,"After");}

findings.validation_status: Reproduced against the actual compiled domain implementation; no source modifications.
